children: U.S. stocks moved lower Wednesday as a surge in oil prices and persistently elevated Treasury yields pressured interest-rate-sensitive sectors, with Brent crude breaking above $100 a barrel amid continued U.S.-Iran tensions.
“Brent crude prices and persistently rising U.S. Treasury yields weigh on stock markets on Wednesday,” Seeking Alpha analyst Chris Lau, of Investing Group Leader for
, stated.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average
fell -0.7%, while the S&P 500 (
) declined -0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite
dropped -0.6%.
Lau said investors responded by selling shares of companies carrying significant debt or those particularly sensitive to higher borrowing costs.
Telecommunications stocks were among the notable decliners, with Comcast
leading the sector lower. Charter Communications
, Verizon
, AT&T
and T-Mobile
also finished down.
Financial companies were similarly pressured, as asset managers Ares Management
, Blackstone
and KKR
fell between 2.5% and nearly 4% during the session.
The weakness came as Brent crude
climbed above the psychologically important $100 threshold, raising concerns that higher energy costs could add to inflationary pressures and complicate the interest-rate outlook.
Meanwhile, rising Treasury yields continued to weigh on equity valuations, particularly for businesses dependent on financing or vulnerable to higher rates.
The combination of escalating geopolitical tensions, expensive oil and elevated yields left investors increasingly cautious.

title: SA analyst: $100 oil and rising yields hammer stocks
